Subject: Request: admin activity logs for SIG / SOC2 evidence

Hi Avery,

We're working through the SIG questionnaire and the auditor has asked for a scoped extract of "admin activity" for a rolling 90-day period plus an on-demand snapshot for the last 12 months. They specifically want: 
- all user/admin login events (success/failure)
- privilege elevation events (role grants, permission changes)
- service account key/credential lifecycle events (create/rotate/revoke)
- API key usage and token issuance logs (where available)
- changes to ACLs and RBAC groups

Questions from our side: format (CSV, JSONL, Parquet), timezone normalization, pseudonymization/redaction guidance for tenant IDs, and an attested manifest (HMAC + checksums) for each bundle. Ideally we can accept daily increments to S3 and a one-off certified snapshot for the 12-month ask.

Do you have a recommended export playbook we can include in our SIG response (we need language around retention/backfill and sampling)? Also please confirm any limitations around PII in event payloads.

Thanks,
Susan
Susan Langston
Compliance Manager, Novamed

Hi all —

Technical proposal below (high level) and I've attached a sample manifest + snippet: export_manifest_template.csv and sample_admin_event_snippet.jsonl.

1) Scope and schema - We will include events tagged as admin.* and auth.* (login, session_start/end, privilege_grant/revoke, api_key.create/rotate/revoke, role.update, acl.change). Each line is a single event with the following canonical fields: event_id, timestamp_utc, event_type, actor_id (hashed), actor_role, target_resource, change_summary, source_ip (redacted at /24 by default for exports), raw_payload (omitted for SIG unless requested).

2) Formats and delivery - Supported export formats: JSONL (default), CSV (for compatibility), Parquet (for large snapshots). Delivery: S3 PUT to presigned path with server-side encryption (AES256) and an accompanying manifest file that includes file_name, record_count, first_timestamp, last_timestamp, sha256_checksum, hmac_signature. HMAC key will be exchanged via our standard secure channel (DocuSign KMS handshake suggested).

3) Retention and sampling - Rolling 90-day extracts are available as a time-windowed query. We can produce an on-demand 12-month snapshot; for costume/performance reasons we may sample high-volume ephemeral events (session.ping) at a 1% rate unless the auditor requires full fidelity. We'll document any sampling in the manifest and SIG response.

4) Pseudonymization/redaction - By default we will hash tenant_id and actor_id with a rotating salt (per-request) and remove user_email from exported payloads. Source IPs will be truncated to /24. If Novamed requires unhashed identifiers for correlation, we'll require a data-processing addendum and an explicit legal approval.

5) Attestation and checksums - Each export will contain a signed manifest (SHA256 + HMAC) and a signed statement of scope (first/last timestamp). For SOC2/attestation needs we can provide a notarized statement from our compliance team on request (requires 3 business days to prepare).

Next: Marissa, can you capture the manifest template into the SIG response doc? Kimberly, please review the pseudonymization language below and advise if it's acceptable for SIG/CAT F.

-Karthik

We reviewed Karthik's proposal and confirmed the following for SIG/CAIQ language: 
- "Admin activity" exports will be provided as described; by default we pseudonymize tenant and user identifiers and document any sampling.
- Exports will include an attested manifest and checksums; delivery via S3 is the standard agreed pathway for evidence handoff.
- For auditors that require raw identifiers for reconciliation, we will provide a limited scope of unhashed identifiers under a signed DPA addendum and with a security review.

Please let us know if you want the Parquet snapshot included as part of the initial evidence or staged after the auditor's request. If Novamed is okay with initial JSONL + manifest daily increments and a single Parquet snapshot for the 12-month window, we'll schedule the export and share access instructions (S3 path + key exchange) and add the export playbook to the SIG response bundle.
